section_summary: This section details diplomatic negotiations and administrative determinations between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the Japanese Embassy concerning reciprocal Federal income tax exemptions for non-diplomatic Japanese officials stationed in the United States under the Act of August 27, 1935. The correspondence addresses statutory criteria, Treasury regulations, and State Department certifications for extensive rosters of Japanese naval, military, railway, financial, and agricultural representatives, as well as claims for tax refunds and bond cancellations. It also documents the State Department's refusal to grant tax-exempt status to an official of the Japanese Tourist Bureau in Los Angeles because the United States maintained no comparable government agency abroad, incorporating related congressional bills and committee reports on the proposed United States Travel Commission.

subfiles.about: Provisional draft note proposing reciprocal income tax exemptions for official compensation of government employees.
subfiles.summary: Provisional Japanese draft note: Japan's Finance Department will exempt US non-diplomatic employees and consular officers from tax on official salaries, subject to non-Japanese nationality, similar services and reciprocity.
subfiles.title: Draft Note from the Japanese Ambassador to the Secretary of State Regarding Reciprocal Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the Japanese Embassy's provisional draft note and the State Department's proposed draft reply to the Treasury Department for review.
subfiles.from: Under Secretary of State William Phillips
subfiles.summary: Phillips sends Treasury the Japanese provisional draft note and State's proposed reply, asking comments on exempting non-diplomatic foreign government employees.
subfiles.title: Letter from Under Secretary of State William Phillips to Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge
subfiles.to: Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of State Department letter transmitting draft notes on reciprocal tax exemption and promising Treasury comments shortly.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Coolidge says the draft notes on tax exemptions are under active consideration and comments will follow within days.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Report on discussions with Treasury officials regarding the draft notes on reciprocal income tax exemption, with attached revised drafts.
subfiles.from: William R. Vallance, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Vallance reports to Hackworth on his conference with Treasury attorneys Swayze and McKirdy regarding the proposed exchange of notes with Japan under the Act of August 27, 1935. The officials agreed on retaining the phrase 'foreign countries' and establishing that the reciprocal exemption does not require American personnel to be continuously stationed in Japan. They also discussed administrative procedures, including State Department certification and Treasury amending Section 641 of Regulations 77 to publish exempt nations in the Cumulative Bulletin. Attached to the memorandum are McKirdy's revised drafts of the State Department reply and the Japanese Embassy note showing proposed modifications and bracketed deletions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from William R. Vallance to Green H. Hackworth, with Revised Draft Notes

subfiles.about: Transmittal of State Department-approved revisions of draft notes on reciprocal income tax exemption to Treasury.
subfiles.from: William R. Vallance, Assistant to the Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Vallance sends Swayze revised draft notes, keeping 'foreign countries' for broader meaning and accepting 'such exemption to continue as long as', with temporary leave not ending exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from William R. Vallance to J. C. Swayze
subfiles.to: J. C. Swayze, Attorney, General Counsel's Office, Bureau of Internal Revenue

subfiles.about: Recommendation to withdraw the draft exchange of notes with Japan following an interdepartmental conference with Treasury officials.
subfiles.from: William R. Vallance, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Vallance reports Treasury officials agreed an exchange of notes only with Japan would be inadvisable unless similar notes went to Britain and others, and submits a letter withdrawing the drafts.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from William R. Vallance to Green H. Hackworth and Eugene H. Dooman
subfiles.to: Green H. Hackworth, Legal Adviser, and Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Formal withdrawal of proposed draft notes concerning reciprocal income tax exemption for Japanese non-diplomatic employees.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State William Phillips
subfiles.summary: Phillips tells Morgenthau that after interdepartmental discussions State withdraws the proposed draft notes on exempting non-diplomatic foreign employees.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State William Phillips to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.

subfiles.about: Confirmation by Treasury that the State Department's request regarding draft notes on tax exemption is treated as withdrawn.
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge
subfiles.summary: Treasury confirms the draft exchange of notes is treated as withdrawn, following the October 29, 1935 conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Treasury T. Jefferson Coolidge to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Discussion with Japanese Embassy Second Secretary Kawahara regarding Federal income tax exemption for Japanese railway officials.
subfiles.from: William T. Turner, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Kawahara asks Turner about tax exemption for Japanese railway officials; Turner advises a formal Embassy note listing officials, duties and taxes assessed, with State certifying under the Act.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Second Secretary Kawahara and William T. Turner

subfiles.about: Request for Federal income tax exemption for Japanese government officials in New York, with an enclosed roster of personnel.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 50 lists New York officials (naval, railway, tobacco monopoly, financial commission, army) seeking tax exemption on a reciprocal basis, certified as Japanese nationals.
subfiles.title: Note No. 50 from Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, with List of Officials in New York

subfiles.about: Formal certification under the Act of August 27, 1935, requesting income tax exemption for Japanese officials listed in Embassy Note No. 50.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Public Law 374 for the officials in Note No. 50 and asks Treasury to grant exemptions and notify collectors.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Japanese Embassy Note No. 50 regarding tax exemption for Japanese officials in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Saito's Note No. 50 and says it was referred to authorities for favorable action.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Internal routing note regarding notes received from the Japanese Embassy on tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's routing slip of March 25, 1936 on incoming Japanese Embassy notes about income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip Regarding Notes on Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Internal routing note forwarding the additional list of Japanese officials seeking tax exemption for review.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip of March 21, 1936 forwarding the additional list of Japanese officials seeking tax exemption to Far Eastern Affairs for comment.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip Regarding Additional List of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: Submission of an additional list of Japanese officials seeking income tax exemption and sailing permits at U.S. ports.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 54 adds officials (naval, agriculture, Formosa, language officers) to Note No. 50 and asks names be sent to collectors at New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Seattle.
subfiles.title: Note No. 54 from Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, with Additional Lists of Officials

subfiles.about: Formal certification under the Act of August 27, 1935, requesting tax exemption for additional Japanese officials listed in Embassy Note No. 54.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under the August 27, 1935 Act for Note No. 54's additional officials and asks Treasury to grant exemption.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Japanese Embassy Note No. 54 transmitting an additional list of officials seeking tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Saito's Note No. 54 of March 19, 1936 and says it was referred to federal authorities.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Account of conference with Second Secretary Kawahara regarding the draft note on exemption for Japanese railway officials.
subfiles.from: William R. Vallance, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Vallance reports Turner brought Kawahara with a draft note on tax exemption; Treasury's September 5, 1935 letter recognized railway officials' exemption.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from William R. Vallance to Green H. Hackworth Regarding Exemption of Japanese Railway Officials

subfiles.about: Internal Department of State routing slip from the Office of the Legal Adviser.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's routing slip (file sheet 218) filed with correspondence on Japanese tax exemptions.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip

subfiles.about: Request for refund of income taxes paid and cancellation of surety bonds filed by Japanese officials in New York, with enclosed roster.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 55 lists officials who filed bonds or paid taxes in New York and asks bond cancellation and refunds; Japan's Treasury exempted American officials.
subfiles.title: Note No. 55 from Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, with Refund List

subfiles.about: Statement that Japan never levied taxes on salaries of American officials during the period Japanese officials were taxed in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Saito's Note No. 60 confirms Japan never taxed American officials in Japan while Japanese officials in the US were taxed.
subfiles.title: Note No. 60 from Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Japanese Embassy notes regarding tax refunds and confirmation of reciprocal tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Notes No. 55 and No. 60 and says bond cancellation and tax refunds were referred to federal authorities.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Certification under the Act of August 27, 1935, requesting cancellation of surety bonds and tax refunds for Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity and asks Treasury to cancel the surety bonds, refund taxes paid, and ensure future exemption for the listed Japanese officials.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Treasury Henry Morgenthau, Jr.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of excerpt from Treasury Department letter regarding tax refunds and bond cancellations to the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State refers to Japanese Embassy Notes No. 55 and No. 60 regarding tax refunds and bond cancellations for Japanese officials. He encloses for the Ambassador's information an excerpt from a Treasury Department letter dated June 4, 1936, addressing the matter.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Request to add Tourist Bureau Secretary Iwawo Yokota to the roster of Japanese officials exempt from income tax.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 62 asks adding Iwawo Yokota of the Tourist Bureau of the Japanese Government Railways, Los Angeles, to the exemption list.
subfiles.title: Note No. 62 from Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito to Secretary of State Cordell Hull

subfiles.about: Refusal to extend income tax exemption to Tourist Bureau Secretary Iwawo Yokota due to lack of a comparable American agency abroad.
subfiles.summary: Hull tells Saito State cannot extend exemption to Yokota because the US has no comparable agency abroad.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State Cordell Hull to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Recommendation that tax exemption be denied to Tourist Bureau official Iwawo Yokota because no equivalent American government agency exists.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs says State cannot certify American officials perform duties similar to Yokota's, since the Japanese Tourist Bureau sells transportation, and recommends refusing exemption.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to the Office of the Legal Adviser

subfiles.about: Cancelled draft letter proposing certification of tax exemption for Tourist Bureau Secretary Iwawo Yokota.
subfiles.summary: Cancelled draft letter to Treasury proposing certification of Iwawo Yokota's exemption, discarded as no equivalent American agency exists.
subfiles.title: Cancelled Draft Letter from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury Regarding Iwawo Yokota

subfiles.about: Transmittal of legislative materials on the proposed United States Travel Commission to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's routing slip forwarding Travel Commission legislation to Far Eastern Affairs to assess government travel agencies.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip Regarding Travel Commission Legislation

subfiles.about: House committee report recommending passage with amendments of S. 33 to establish a Travel Division in the Department of Commerce.
subfiles.from: Clarence F. Lea, House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce
keywords: House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce
Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: House Report 2254 recommends S. 33 as amended by H.R. 5844, creating a Travel Division in Commerce; notes 57 foreign government travel bureaus in New York and no US counterpart abroad.
subfiles.title: House Report No. 2254 (74th Cong., 2d Sess.): United States Travel Commission (to accompany S. 33)

subfiles.about: Senate committee report recommending passage of S. 33 creating an independent United States Travel Commission.
subfiles.from: Royal S. Copeland, Senate Committee on Commerce
subfiles.summary: Senate Report 999 favors S. 33 creating a US Travel Commission of the Secretaries of State and Commerce to promote foreign travel, citing an 8-to-1 spending imbalance.
subfiles.title: Senate Report No. 999 (74th Cong., 1st Sess.): United States Travel Commission (to accompany S. 33)

subfiles.about: Printed text of Senate bill S. 33 as passed by the Senate and reported with committee amendments in the House.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: The printed legislative text of S. 33 shows the bill as passed by the Senate on August 16, 1935, creating an independent United States Travel Commission composed of the Secretaries of State and Commerce, alongside the strike-through amendment reported by the House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce. The House amendment substitutes provisions directing the Secretary of Commerce to establish a Travel Division within the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce. The bill details administrative powers, personnel appointments, foreign representative allowances, and authorized appropriations.
subfiles.title: Senate Bill S. 33 (74th Cong., 2d Sess.): An Act to Encourage Travel to and Within the United States by Citizens of Foreign Countries

subfiles.about: House committee report recommending passage of H.R. 5844 to establish a Tourist Travel Division in the Department of Commerce.
subfiles.from: Clarence F. Lea, House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: House Report 1500 favors H.R. 5844 creating a Tourist Travel Division in Commerce, preferred by Secretary Roper over S. 33's commission, to reduce unfavorable payment balances.
subfiles.title: House Report No. 1500 (74th Cong., 1st Sess.): To Encourage Travel to and Within the United States (to accompany H.R. 5844)

subfiles.about: Printed text of House bill H.R. 5844 authorizing the establishment of a Tourist Travel Division in the Department of Commerce.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: The printed text of H.R. 5844 provides for establishing a Tourist Travel Division within the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce under the Department of Commerce. It authorizes the Division to prepare and disseminate travel promotional material, cooperate with carriers and private organizations, appoint foreign representatives, and authorizes annual appropriations of up to $75,000 for fiscal year 1936 and $125,000 thereafter.
subfiles.title: House Bill H.R. 5844 (74th Cong., 1st Sess.): A Bill to Encourage Travel to and Within the United States, and for Other Purposes

subfiles.about: Internal routing note regarding correspondence to the Japanese Embassy on tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser's routing slip of April 22, 1936 on proposed correspondence to the Japanese Embassy about income tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip Regarding Japanese Embassy Correspondence

subfiles.about: Treasury Department review of State Department certification regarding tax exemption for Japanese officials under the Act of August 27, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Treasury acknowledges Note No. 50 and State's reciprocity certification, and quotes Section 116(h) of the Revenue Act of 1934 as amended by Public Law 374.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Secretary of the Treasury to the Secretary of State Regarding Tax Exemption for Japanese Officials
